Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: visual-bible model sheet, original editorial paper-craft adaptation of a localized Amazonian narrative; not a traditional Indigenous artwork or an ethnographic reconstruction.
Style/medium: sophisticated tangible 3D cut-paper world, matte dyed paper and cardstock, broad hand-cut shapes, sparse folds, separated physical layers at different distances, crisp inner paper edges, soft projected shadows and real air between planes. Faces use a restrained few nearly flat paper pieces, minimal eyes, natural human proportions. Build depth mainly between layers of the world, not by faceting heads. Every depicted surface including water, vegetation, ground, clothing and atmosphere must be paper.
Palette continuity: deep foliage green #385745, young green #8C9B58, burnt terracotta #B95737, river blue-grey #304852, pale fibre #CBB389, earth brown #806348, charcoal #343733, restrained warm paper #F3EBDD. This is the project's editorial palette, not a traditional colour code.
Framing: immersive edge-to-edge full bleed, composed deliberately to all four limits. Full bodies of the subjects must be complete with breathing room. World layers continue outside the image edges; no visible perimeter of a model, backing board, table, pedestal, cardboard foundation, exhibition platform, vignette outline, frame or mockup. No text, labels, lettering, logos, numbers, arrows or watermark. Details can be arranged as separate views without panels or dividing lines, over a continuous contextual paper world.
Avoid: photorealistic wood or sand, shiny plastic, CGI toy faces, giant heads, kawaii, polygonal low-poly heads, golden aura, luminous runes, European fantasy, generic tribal ornament, copied body-paint patterns, enormous feather headdresses, pan-Indigenous costume, exposed genitalia, sexualisation, gore, explicit violence. Depict only the requested subjects; no added mythical companions. Respect natural anatomy; human hands have five fingers, birds have bird wings and feet, snakes have no limbs.

Primary request: Nofïdeño, the Mother who supports the earth. Make an identity sheet with three complete full-body views of the SAME mature adult woman: frontal on the left, side profile in the middle, back on the right. All three heads and both feet fully visible. Same medium-brown paper skin, calm narrow adult face, black shoulder-length hair, plain calf-length terracotta paper tunic, charcoal narrow sash, bare feet. The clothing, face and exact age are our reversible editorial design, not claimed customary dress. Each view approximately 58 percent of image height, not a giant woman towering over people. On her bent left shoulder rests the same shallow folded earth-and-river paper landscape, like a folded mantle of land, clearly supported by her shoulder and hand. It is an editorial way to represent carrying the world, NOT a spherical globe, trophy, basket or decorative crown. Allow her posture and supporting arm to explain the weight. Behind and below these views a continuous receding paper forest, broad earth layers and a quiet river fill the canvas edges. Keep her human silhouette readable and the supported landscape secondary. No baby, other gods, fertility anatomy, constellations or extra fruit decoration.

Primary request: the HUMAN base identity of Dïïjoma, not his transformations. Three complete full-body views of the exact same adult man, approximately forty years old: front, side profile and back, each 60 percent of image height, all heads, hands and bare feet completely in frame. Lean adult build, medium-brown matte paper skin, short straight black hair, restrained angular narrow face, clean-shaven, natural proportions. Plain knee-length dark foliage-green paper tunic with short sleeves and a narrow charcoal sash; unadorned, a reversible editorial garment rather than claimed traditional attire. Maintain exactly the same cut, sash, hair and proportions in every view. Arms relaxed, hands simple and anatomically coherent. A continuous quiet riverbank made of large matte earth and water paper layers extends to all image edges, with sparse receding forest planes and visible depth gaps. Primary request: a STATE MODEL sheet for the aquatic boa exteriorized from Dïïjoma's power. Dominant complete large serpent occupies the lower two thirds, from rounded snake head through a broad heavy sinuous coiled body to tapered tail; the ENTIRE snake must be readable without any cropped endpoint. Build its body from overlapping broad olive-green and charcoal paper segments, matte dark oval saddles, pale warm-paper underside, plausible snake head with small dark eyes; no horns, legs, moustache, dragon features or glowing mouth. In upper-right show the same boa in intermediate size, entirely visible, passing along a lagoon edge. The pot is its narrative vessel, not a display stand. Primary request: a full-bodied BIRD transformation model of Dïïjoma, anchored in the source's harpy eagle identification. On the left show the entire perched eagle, feet through crest in frame; on the right show the exact SAME eagle flying with both full wings and tail uncropped, its full wingspan occupying 55 percent of canvas width. Grey crested eagle head, strong hooked dark beak, small charcoal eyes with a dark charcoal-paper area around them, slate-grey back and wing upper surfaces, pale chest, thick feathered legs. Continuous receding forest canopy and quiet distant maloca roof planes fill the full-bleed background; internal paper layers cast shadows with air and depth, not a pale isolated display board.

Primary request: a GROUP GRAMMAR study of collective participation and renewal, six complete adult human bodies in one loose shallow arc inside a paper maloca. This is explicitly our contemporary comparative study of everyday-clothed participants, not a reconstruction of the primordial people's costume and not an invented named ritual. Three adult women and three adult men, approximately ages 25 to 65, distinct natural builds and modest adult faces, medium-brown paper skin, diverse straight black or greying hair. Contemporary plain short-sleeve T-shirts or blouses and long trousers or a modest long plain skirt; muted foliage green, warm-paper cream, river-blue and terracotta, varied clothing for individuals, no uniform. Hands loosely connected for some adjacent people, others listening with relaxed hands, subtle coordinated weight shift; no claimed specific dance step. Full-bleed layered paper timber posts, high roof underside, deep earth floor and a softly lit rear opening make a spacious continuous world. No headdress, face paint, nudity, ceremonial masks, drums, spears, extra people, costumes copied from another Indigenous nation, or photographic clothing textures.

Primary request: an OBJECT MODEL sheet of a pair of maguaré wooden slit drums, NOT membrane drums.
